title: Anderson orthogonality scaling in the Rabi-driven heavy Fermi polaron
abstract: The Anderson orthogonality catastrophe (AOC) is a paradigmatic many-body phenomenon in which a local perturbation induces a macroscopic response of a Fermi sea. We probe signatures of the AOC by coherently driving heavy Fermi polarons in an ultracold $^6$Li-$^{133}$Cs mixture. We observe a power-law dependence of the measured Rabi frequency on the drive strength, with exponents consistent with AOC predictions. Finite-temperature simulations quantitatively reproduce the observed scaling, indicating that AOC signatures persist beyond the idealized zero-temperature, infinite-mass limit. The damping of the Rabi oscillations provides access to polaron dephasing and reveals a nonmonotonic drive dependence, qualitatively consistent with current theories. Our results establish coherently driven impurities as a versatile probe of quantum many-body dynamics through local coherent control.

bite.hook: We observed a power-law dependence of the measured Rabi frequency on the drive strength, consistent with AOC predictions.
tldr: Probed signatures of the Anderson orthogonality catastrophe by coherently driving heavy Fermi polarons in an ultracold Li-Cs mixture.
Used a mixture of ultracold lithium-6 and cesium-133 atoms with finite-temperature simulations to test theoretical predictions.
Found power-law dependence in Rabi frequencies and nonmonotonic drive dependence in polaron dephasing.
bite.whyItMatters: Understanding how quantum many-body systems react to local disturbances helps physicists build better quantum technologies and study fundamental material properties.
bite.eli5: Imagine a heavy bowling ball dropped into a calm swimming pool, causing waves across the entire pool. Physicists did something very similar with tiny quantum atoms to see how one disturbed particle ripples through a whole crowd of others.

glossary.shortDef: A many-body phenomenon where a local perturbation induces a macroscopic response of a Fermi sea.
glossary.eli5Def: When poking one tiny particle causes a huge reaction across an entire crowd of particles.

glossary.shortDef: A quasiparticle formed when an impurity interacts with a surrounding Fermi sea of particles.
glossary.eli5Def: A foreign object moving through a dense crowd, dragging some of the crowd along with it.
